classification.difficultyReason: Read the vertices from the grid, identify the horizontal side directly, and use rise and run to calculate the two sloping lengths. Then sum the lengths, apply the map scale and round; these are routine linked applications of the taught method.

content.prompt: A block of land is shown on this map. Each unit distance represents 100 metres in real life. Calculate the perimeter of the block to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Unshaded triangular land boundary on a unit coordinate grid from −4 to 4 on both axes. Both axes have arrows at each end and numbered ticks −3, −2, −1, 1, 2, 3. The Cartesian-origin O label is omitted under the house graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (−2,2), (3,2), (2,−2); horizontal top side of length 5 units; remaining side lengths √17 and √32 units. Each unit represents 100 metres.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied map and unlabelled vertex markers are visible; no lengths or perimeter are supplied.

answer.worked:
The horizontal side is $5$ units. Using rise and run for the other two sides:
$$\begin{align*}
d_1 &= \sqrt{(-4)^2+(-1)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{17}\text{ units} \\
d_2 &= \sqrt{4^2+(-4)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{32}\text{ units} \\
P &= 100(5+\sqrt{17}+\sqrt{32})\text{ m} \\
&\approx 1478\text{ m}
\end{align*}$$
The perimeter is $1478\text{ m}$ to the nearest metre.
